defects.description: The B2B authentication decision remains unanswered: R16 is still a question, and no application authentication or authorization mechanism is described. WAF request filtering does not establish client identity or tenant authorization.

Specify security-group relationships allowing only the ALB to reach tasks and only tasks to reach PostgreSQL and the cache, together with least-privilege task and execution roles; private placement alone does not define these controls.

Make the ECS service configuration explicit: maintain tasks across both AZs, configure health checks and sufficient surviving-zone capacity, and handle database and cache reconnections after failover.

The connection notation is misleading in two places: WAF should be associated with the ALB rather than presented as a separately invoked HTTPS endpoint, and tasks pull images from ECR rather than ECR initiating delivery.
The claim that sessions survive an AZ loss needs qualification because Redis-compatible replication is asynchronous and failover can lose recent session writes.

Identify the credential-rotation implementation and explain how application connections obtain refreshed credentials; storing and rotating a secret does not by itself refresh credentials already cached by the application.

reviews.summary: A well-matched, reasonably economical Multi-AZ container architecture covers the explicit requirements but needs a concrete authentication decision and clearer operational and security configuration.

defects.description: The REST API integration with the internal ALB omits the required VPC link and private-integration configuration. The illustrated forwarding edges alone do not provide connectivity into the VPC.

The RDS Proxy authentication path is incomplete: no proxy access to the stored database secret or alternative database-authentication configuration is shown, and the task-to-proxy authentication method is not selected. Placing a proxy between the application and database does not establish these credentials automatically.

Clarify that the REST API uses a Cognito user-pool authorizer with appropriate resource-server scopes for client-credentials access tokens; 'Cognito client-credentials authorizer' is not a distinct authorizer type.

Specify the ECS service's minimum cross-AZ task placement, surviving-zone capacity, security-group boundaries, least-privilege IAM roles, and encrypted database/cache connections rather than relying solely on private-subnet placement.

API Gateway, an internal ALB, RDS Proxy, and Aurora introduce additional cost and configuration compared with a simpler ALB-and-RDS baseline; explain the workload or API-management needs that justify each addition.

reviews.summary: B provides an explicit machine-to-machine authentication choice and a plausible HA stack, but its private API integration and proxy authentication are incomplete and its additional components need stronger justification.

defects.description: R13 promises duplicate-free email delivery on reruns, but no durable per-report/per-recipient delivery state or deduplication workflow is described. Deterministic S3 keys do not prevent duplicate emails after a partial failure or repeated task launch.

For the public-subnet Fargate approach, explicitly enable a task public IP and internet-gateway routing, deny unsolicited inbound traffic, and scope task permissions; public-subnet placement alone does not establish outbound connectivity.

Presigned URLs are transferable bearer credentials, not recipient-bound authorization. State that forwarded links remain usable until expiration and account for the signing task credentials' lifetime when selecting link validity.

Define the schedule's time zone, launch-failure retry/DLQ behavior, and a completion-or-missing-success alarm. Scheduler delivery success does not demonstrate that the 25-minute task completed successfully.
Include SES sender verification, production access where required, and handling of throttling or failed sends so emailing all 40 managers is an explicit deployment prerequisite.

reviews.summary: A is a simple and cost-conscious fit for the 25-minute nightly job, with remaining gaps around deduplication, task networking, delivery readiness, and the limits of emailed bearer links.

defects.description: The private-subnet Fargate task has no specified NAT route or suitable VPC endpoints for image retrieval and its S3, SES, and logging calls. An explicit outbound-access design is required, and its cost must be included.

No database authentication or credential-delivery mechanism is selected for the reporting task. Define a read-only database identity and securely supply its credentials, or explicitly configure an alternative such as supported IAM database authentication.
For the HTTP API, specify a JWT authorizer using the Cognito issuer and intended audience rather than leaving the configuration as a REST-style 'Cognito user pool' authorizer.

The emailed-link sign-in experience is incomplete: identify the landing page or client that performs sign-in and submits the resulting token to the download API, and restrict access to provisioned manager identities.

The Cognito, API Gateway, Lambda, and sign-in client introduce an additional application to build and maintain; justify this against the simple-and-cheap requirement rather than treating authenticated downloads as cost-free complexity.
Specify the schedule time zone, task completion and missing-run alarms, launch-failure handling, and a rerun strategy that avoids unnecessary duplicate emails.

reviews.summary: B selects suitable long-running serverless compute and stronger download authentication, but omits essential task connectivity and database authentication while adding a comparatively complex download application.

defects.description: R10 promises prompt content updates, but no cache TTL, Cache-Control policy, or invalidation procedure is specified; uploading replacement files does not immediately refresh cached CloudFront responses.
Explicitly configure the viewer protocol policy to redirect HTTP to HTTPS or require HTTPS, and use the S3 REST origin with OAC rather than an S3 website endpoint.
Identify the alarm notification destination and keep alarm count and noncurrent object-version retention bounded so optional monitoring and versioning remain consistent with the small monthly budget.

reviews.summary: A is a strong low-cost static-site design with correctly located TLS certification, private OAC-backed storage, and scoped staff access, needing only small caching and operational refinements.

defects.description: The bucket is declared private, but no OAC/OAI origin authentication or bucket policy authorizing CloudFront is specified. HTTPS origin requests alone do not grant CloudFront access to private objects.
The ACM certificate is placed in an unspecified Primary Region; explicitly require us-east-1 for the certificate attached to CloudFront, regardless of the bucket's Region.
The staff upload path does not define authenticated, least-privilege access limited to the website content; add an explicit IAM-based access arrangement.
Specify cache lifetimes or an invalidation procedure for menu and opening-hours updates, because replacing an S3 object does not immediately replace previously cached responses.

reviews.summary: B uses the right inexpensive hosting services and explicitly redirects HTTP, but leaves private-origin authorization, the CloudFront certificate Region, and staff access insufficiently specified.

preference.why: A meets the explicit hosting, availability, egress, and rotation requirements with fewer components and a clearer ingress path; B adds cost and leaves its VPC-link and proxy-authentication integrations incomplete.

A better matches the simple-and-cheap priority through a single scheduled Fargate job, direct email delivery, and an explicit credential store; B adds a download application while omitting essential private-task connectivity.
Both choose an appropriate low-cost static stack, but A explicitly supplies OAC, the required us-east-1 certificate placement, and scoped staff access.
